turns.text: Good to see you again. Where would you like to start today?
I made myself a cup of tea this morning and just stood by the window for a while.
I see. Can you say a bit more?
My husband Tom is a paramedic and works night shifts, so I am alone with the baby most nights.
Mm-hm. Go on.
The journey here took a while, but at least I had time to gather my thoughts. It is not easy to talk about.
What happened next?
Some days are better than others, and I try to remind myself of that when things get heavy.
What happened next?
I get up six or seven times a night just to check that Oliver is still breathing.
And how was that for you?
It is strange to sit here and say all of this out loud, but it does help a little. It is not easy to talk about.
How did that feel for you?
My son Oliver is five months old and I have been anxious every single day since he was born.
And how was that for you?
I had a long day yesterday and I was so tired in the evening that I just sat in front of the television. I think so, yes.
What went through your mind then?
I wrote a few notes before coming here, but now I cannot remember half of what I wanted to say.
What went through your mind then?
My mum lives in Aberdeen and I am in Bristol, so she cannot just pop round.
Tell me more about that.
I am not sure where to begin, there are so many things going round in my head at the moment. It is not easy to talk about.
Tell me more about that.
The train was late again this morning, so I almost did not make it on time today.
We are nearly out of time. Is there anything you want to add?
No, I think that is everything. Thank you.
